newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities just shy of record highs in IBIS.
newsitem.headline: German equities just shy of record highs in IBIS.

text.p: German shares were just shy of record highs in afternoon IBIS trade on Thursday, boosted by ongoing strength in the dollar and firmer German debt markets and U.S. producer price data calming inflation fears.
At 1332 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 16.55 points at 2,585.25. The record high for the IBIS DAX is 2,589.91 points, which it hit on July 11.
The DAX ended bourse trade up 3.52 points at 2,570.32.
"The afternoon has gone a lot better for us and I'm pretty bullish at the moment. The dollar is right for us, Bunds are helping and I think we could see records soon," said a trader.

"We've been going sideways for a long time, consolidating, but we're entering a bullish period. If we don't hit records today, we'll do it tomorrow or early next week and then the next stop is at 2,600 points," said a Frankfurt trader.
"There is new cash coming into the market with people switching out of other investments," said the trader.
Dealers said that volumes of late had also been better, which they viewed as encouraging.
One of the top performers in afternoon trade was Deutsche Bank AG, which was boosted by an upgrade by Swiss bank UBS earlier in the day.
Deutsche Bank shares were up 82 pfennigs at 71.95 marks in late afternoon trade and was the top share by volume.
The market started to rise in a notable fashion after U.S. PPI figures for August registered a 0.3 percent rise, after the July figure was unchanged.
Analysts had been looking at a range of up to 0.1 and 0.2 percent and the higher-than-expected increase calmed fears of inflation in the U.S.
